title: plasmashell uses several GB of memory and gets OOM-killed when a calendar plugin removes many events at once (DaysModel resets the model once per removed event)
line: Plasma no longer freezes and runs out of memory when a calendar in the Digital Clock replaces many events at once, as an iCal feed reload does.
explanation: DaysModel::onEventRemoved() reset the whole model once for every removed event, even when the event wasn't shown. A calendar that replaces all its events at once (an Akonadi iCal feed that regenerates UIDs on every download, or removing a calendar) sends hundreds of removals back to back, so the month view rebuilt all 42 day delegates and their event dots hundreds of times without returning to the event loop, and plasmashell grew by ~150 MB/s until the OOM killer took it. The reporter's open MR !7183 (applied unchanged) queues removed uids and applies them in one reset from a queued call, skips the reset when none of them is shown, and flushes pending removals before new or modified data so a moved event (remove + re-add) still ends up right.

commits.message:
calendar: apply event removals in DaysModel in one batch

Each removed event reset the whole model, so a calendar that replaces
many events at once rebuilt the month view per event until plasmashell
ran out of memory. Removals are now queued and applied in one reset.

BUG: 526769

media.caption: Pure master, Digital Clock popup opened once: a test calendar plugin removes its 176 events and re-adds them with new uids. plasmashell climbs from 0.43 GB to 2.9 GB and is OOM-killed (3 GB cap) after 20 s.
Same reload with the fix: memory stays flat at ~450 MB and the whole update takes about 0.2 s.
The clock popup on pure master right before the reload (176 test events, 4 of them today).
The popup after the reload with the fix: same events and dots, nothing missing or doubled.

Regression check with the fix: one of today's events is moved to tomorrow with the same uid (remove + re-add). Top: before the move; bottom: Lesson 10 left today's agenda and a red dot appeared on the 22nd.

review.text: Applies the reporter's open MR !7183 unchanged: removals are batched into one queued reset, skipped when nothing shown is affected, and flushed before new or modified data so moved events stay right. It fixes the actual cause (one model reset per removed event), and the rig shows the OOM storm become a flat 163 ms update with moved/removed-event regressions checked.
